name: inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-pulp-timer-zipdma-4w-compressed-f1f6
notes: trigger_writes and status_offsets repeat the values already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-irq-pulp-timer-profile.json; the entry re-checks them against the timer register map and interrupt declarations
dma_window must not overlap the APB target window; the timer owns 0x40000000..0x40000fff
the timer declares 50 MHz, the CPU 50 MHz and the ZipDMA a nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models

f1_program_words 4 declares a four-record-word F1 program in the fixed trampoline slot and f1_allow_compressed admits two-parcel compressed record words: a record word whose bits [1:0] are not 11 is two 16-bit parcels, the low half executing at pc and the high half at pc + 2, and a 32-bit instruction still occupies a whole record word (it may not straddle one).  Only the safe straight-line ALU subset with a destination in x12..x15 is admitted (C.ADDI/C.LI/C.LUI/C.SLLI/C.SRLI/C.SRAI/C.ANDI/C.MV/C.ADD/C.SUB/C.XOR/C.OR/C.AND); compressed control transfers (C.J/C.JAL/C.JR/C.JALR/C.BEQZ/C.BNEZ), compressed loads/stores (C.LW/C.SW/C.LWSP/C.SWSP/C.LD/C.SD/...), the stack-pointer forms, C.EBREAK and the RV64-only forms are refused by name.  Compressed and computed-base address forms are mutually exclusive, and f1_subword is incompatible with both.  A compressed image retires one instruction per parcel, so the case's retirement evidence is the in-slot RVFI trace: prog_retires counts instructions (8 for this 4-word program, not 4), a parcel steps 2 bytes and a 32-bit word steps 4, prog_pc_order is strictly increasing, and prog_trace_hash (FNV-1a 32 over pc/insn/rd/wdata, with insn the 16-bit parcel) is compared with the Python reference trace built from f1_reference_expectation.  Evidence: runs/round1-f1-c/ (fixed-compressed, fuzz-20).
